I called the restaurant to inform them of our concerns but she couldn’t really understand me and there wasn’t anyone else I could speak to. It’s a shame because I never like to complain but this is the last time, we will never order again!!

Give your lovely delivery driver a pay rise! Very polite. Gave us a quick call to say he was 5 minutes away. A simple bit of communication makes all the difference! Pizza was delicious and huge! Thank you 😊

Absolutely delicious Pizza. Great prices. Tasted very very GOOD!
Will be coming here now for my takeaway.

2 hrs still waiting ... no one answering phone. Says delivered but it has not.
I will update when/ if i ever recieve it

[Update] Received after long wait ,some guests had to leave so went home hungry. Got a free bottle of coca cola for long wait. Pizza was hot and everyone enjoyed even the fussy kids lol driver was cool and seemed very sorry. Shop was busy this saturday evening...

We ordered yesterday on JustEat app and were profusely disappointed with what was delivered. 2 cold pizza, one with a hanging dark hair on the base of the pepperoni - I will not attach a picture here as this has already been taken forward differently. I know mistakes happen so I’m trying to understand and think as a business.. but I have just thrown up most of last night as I only realised the hair after eating half of the pizza slice. I am also 7 months pregnant! I do not want to describe how that made me feel but will definitely not return.

I ordered at 2:30pm and didn’t receive the food until 6:30pm - totally unacceptable! The food was obviously completely cold when it arrived. I first called at 4pm and was told the driver wasn’t even at the restaurant yet. I kept calling for updates and kept being told it would arrive “soon”. I appreciated them answering but being told the delay was due to traffic was a bit ridiculous…

I ordered the chicken noodle soup and it was honestly very bland — no taste whatsoever. It felt like just noodles and chicken pieces thrown into hot water. The dumplings were also disappointing; all of them even had a piece of paper sheet still stuck on it (good thing I noticed before eating it). They came with no sauce at all, just plain and flavorless.

On top of that, the food was served in basic plastic packaging that didn’t look very welcoming. For the price they charge, I really expected much better quality. Definitely not worth it.
The owner is super nice, foods are absolutely delicious
Great service and reasonable prices. The food was delicious and arrived very quickly. The bubble tea was also excellent. Highly recommended, whether you dine in or order takeaway.
Feel like doesn’t really worth the price ?
Very good home-style Sichuan food - the ‘Spicy Chicken’ (crispy boneless chicken with chillies, peanuts and Sichuan pepper) and Ma Po Tofu especially.

name: NOKO (Camberwell)
address: 15 Camberwell Church St, London SE5 8TR, UK

reviews.text:
We popped into NOKO based on the excellent reviews we read on Google.

The menu is compact while still offering a nice variety of Asian classics. From Korean fried chicken to smacked cucumbers, Yakitori skewers to pork dumplings, you’re covered!

The service was acceptable but not friendly.

The food came quickly and was well prepared if not exceptional.

It’s worth stopping by for a quick meal.

Came with high expectations given reviews and was not disappointed. The mushroom skewers were fantastic, the smacked cucumber very refreshing, and the noodles deliciously chewy.

It's not the cheapest spot in the area but very reasonable, highly recommend

I’ve been coming to NOKO Camberwell many times and the food is always amazing. The Dan Dan noodles are absolutely the best in the area, and the skewers, spicy cabbage, and broccoli tahini are all fantastic.
However, during my recent visit, I was disappointed with the lady service. The lady who appeared to be in charge was quite rude and shouted at the delivery driver several times. There was no smile and the overall attitude felt unfriendly.
As a loyal customer, this was upsetting to see. I truly love the food here, but I hope the management can address this issue. Good service is just as important as good food, and I would hate to stop supporting a place I enjoy so much.

Wow. Happened across by accident and what a find! Fantastic food, beautifully presented. Its a small, but varied menu with something for everyone. I also love the small, cosy feel, and wonderful service. I shall be back, soon, and bringing friends with me.

This was such a great find that we stumbled across! The food was amazing (special mention to the Dan Dan Noodles, smacked cucumber and literally all of the small plates) and the staff gave me a free cocktail to try - which was delicious! Such a friendly place with lovely staff, amazing food and generally a lovely vibe to it. Highly recommend

name: Little Cellars
address: 75 Camberwell Church St, London SE5 8TU, UK

reviews.text: Really lovely meal and great service. We love Peckham Cellars so were really excited to try our local version and it didn’t disappoint. Such fantastic food, great wine, and the staff made adjustments to the set menu for my gluten free requirements without any issue which is incredibly appreciated. We’ll definitely be back!

lovely little wine bar! Food was nice, but there is room for improvement, the burrata had an excess of pesto and it covers the taste of the actual burrata. The focaccia was lovely so the potatoes + croquetas! good selection of wine as well!

I can’t recommend this place enough, especially when you are in the mood for wine and small plates. The food was incredible and portions are quite generous. The orange wine was so good. I’ll come back for sure
Really amazing find. Excellent service and value for money. Great sharing menu.

So happy to have Little Cellars on the high street. The short food menu has lots to offer - I loved the prawns in a buttery sherry sauce, and the coarse-textured terrine.  Reasonably priced wines by the glass across a range of cépages.  Knowledgeable and straightforward service in a grown-up space. Really good all round.

Absolutely superb tacos and quite reasonably priced too - £5-6 each. The Thai chicken special and the beef birria quesataco (pictured), were particular highlights! Excellent margaritas too. Please open a branch in Forest Hill!
Amazing authentic tacos. We had the birria, baja fish and pibil tacos. They were all great, you probably need more than 3 per person.

A nice restaurant with tasty food. We ordered tacos and beef birria, and both were flavorful. The margaritas were well-crafted as well. Overall, this restaurant is a good choice for a Mexican night out.

Real nice Tacos restaurant and was perfect and exactly what we wanted! Nice menu but sadly a lot of it was sold out, which was a shame maybe because it was later Sunday.

Not a far walk from Peckham Rye station if you're traveling that way, quirky part, nice friendly staff, fresh food and a quick service.

Well worth a try.

Solid A*****

Really impressive! Heard a lot of hype, was not disappointed at all. Great tacos and even better service! The Birria (and broth) was a solid 10/10. Cannot wait to come back 🫱🏽‍🫲🏼

Ive been at Oru / Trinco several times now for breakfast, lunch and dinner.. every meal has been a delight of flavors. I really love the atmosphere of the place and honestly the food it tastes so good that is difficult to resist keep coming back.. I particularly think there is nothing like these food around the area.
The only down side is that if I wish to have breakkie or lunch while getting some work with my compputer done .. finding a space in the area where computers are allowed is tricky and very limited the space to have your plate, coffee and computer.
Price it depends on the meal.. lunch and breakfast can be around £10 pp dinner £30pp and up.

I’ve had breakfast at Trinco three times now and it has been lovely each time. The fruit toppings on their sweet breakfast are seasonal and you get a very generous portion for the price, particularly if you order the bircher muesli (this is my favourite so far). Everything has a Sri Lankan twist which I absolutely love as it sets them apart from the rest of the cafes in Dulwich.
The service is friendly and they have a great yoga studio called Oru at the back where everyone is welcome regardless of their experience!
Excited to try the dinner menu next which has lots of great Sri Lankan dishes and specials that change with the season!!

We had a fantastic experience at Trinco. Great vibes, sensational food and a special shoutout to Liz who was super friendly, attentive & charming and made the whole experience extra fun. Highly recommend!

It's definitely more of a trendy place and I understand the vibe there is not for everyone.
It's busy whenever we go, but the atmosphere is friendly and it's not too noisy. We've been shown to our table every time within 10/15mn after waiting in the high tables section.
The chai latte is delicious and so is the roasted aubergine/ chickpea curry that comes with the thosai. I could have had the dosa by itself because it was very tasty. The maple aubergine on focaccia is not too bad either. I find that the portions are just ok for me but I think for big eaters it might be a bit small. Our waiter last time was a bit distracted so service was a tad slow.

Trico have created a space of wonder and comfortable insight. It’s relaxing and calm and softens the atmosphere of the busy Dulwich Street the staff are friendly calm and very knowledgeable about the food and all things to do with coffee. it’s one of the very few places in London where you can get a coffee after four or even 5 o’clock and I’m talking about high-quality coffee not the usual chain types! The food that I had was delicious fragrant enticing I don’t think I’ve talked so much while I’m eating about the depth the range and the quality of flavours and aromas if you’re anywhere near Dulwich or even miles and miles away you need to pay a visit to this beautiful space they’ve been created by the awesome Trinco team

Having moved back to London from Southern California, the food I missed most was good Mexican food. It’s great to see many New Mexican restaurants popping up but often it can be a hit or miss in terms of authenticity. Today I tried Chilaquilles at Guacamole’s in Peckham and washed it down with a tasty horchata. The taste was authentic and reminded me of the tastes I experienced back in California and Mexico. Definitely worth a visit. 😋

We went on the £9 Tuesdays. Absolutely delicious 🤤 honestly the best mexican in London so far!

An excellent selection in terms of choice, went for 2 x the pork, 1 x chicken and 1 x fish.

The chips and dip, fresh and very moreish.

Lovely staff, the owner is great and coming back for the barrita beef as it was sold out 😭

Highly recommend, super easy to get to. Peckham Rye station is a stone throw away too.

See you again!

Solid A*****

My love of tacos took me all the way to Peckham Rye …. Hidden gem is an under statement🤩🤩 I ordered each taco and even took some away . Amazing staff and the owner was super helpful . Definitely worth the visit .
The best tacos I've had in my life. Grabs beers at local tesco and enjoy the best tacos of your life. We tried most of them beef chicken saucy ones incredible. The smoothest guacamole.

🚇Nunhead
🍺 £6.50 Cruzcampo

The Waverley Arms is located on a quiet residential street next to historic Nunhead Cemetery in southeast London. The nearest station is Nunhead mainline.

This late Victorian pub was built in 1895 and has beautiful leaded frosted windows. As mentioned, the pub sits next to Nunhead Cemetery, one of London’s ‘Magnificent Seven’ Victorian cemeteries, which opened in 1840.

This is a bright and airy, one-bar, two-roomed pub that is traditional at heart with contemporary touches. The servery is centrally located, with the bar forming a “J” shape around it. The decor consists of a boarded floor with chequered tiling around the servery, green half-height wall panels, and lighter-shaded walls above, adorned with colourful photos. There are two fireplaces with mirrors above, and plenty of traditional seating, along with a couple of comfy sofas. Just off the main bar is a good-sized room with an atrium that leads to an intimate walled beer garden, there also some benches at the side of the pub.

There is a good mix of beers available which included two stouts and one cask ale. I kept in simple and opted for a Cruzcampo, my pint was great, price point was a smidge above average. The food menu is hearty British pub classics, fish and chips costs £17.45, roasts are available on a Sunday.

I arrived just after 3 p.m. on a sunny Saturday afternoon in April. The pub was fairly busy, with a mix of drinkers and diners enjoying the chilled, relaxed local pub atmosphere. The service was great — I was served by an upbeat and friendly member of the team who was warm and welcoming.

The pub shows live sport, hosts live music, and holds a pub quiz on Thursdays.

The quiet backstreet location, beautiful Victorian architecture, calming interior, good choice of beers, and friendly service make for an excellent pub experience. What a lovely local pub this is — a must-visit if you’re in the area.

Wonderful local pub and also where we had our wedding party! Douglas and the team were incredible, and kindly let us take up the entire pub for the evening 😀 countless guests were talking about how good the food was and there was plenty of it ☺️ the staff were so helpful and friendly. So many people have told us how they really enjoyed our wedding and what a great time they had. We couldn’t be happier with our day. Our parents had a wonderful time too, and my mother (mother of the bride, if ykyk) had one of the best days of her life and couldn’t rave about The Waverley Arms more if she tried (and trust me, she’s told EVERYONE!!)

Douglas and the team catered for all the dietary requirements of our guests, coeliac, lactose intolerant, vegan, veggies, pescatarian (me ☺️) and even made a whole dish for my sister, who was suffering from a gall stone at the time and could eat no fats/oils, she said she had the tastiest chicken she’d been able to eat in a really long time and was over the moon. Real thanks to the chef 👏🏻 we also had about 10 kids under 10 at the wedding and the pub has board games ready for them to play, and they played out in the courtyard at the back too, they had a great time ☺️

Honestly I could go on and on! So if you’re looking for a venue or just a really friendly pub lunch, get down to The Waverley Arms!! 🤗

Thank you again, Holly and Mico

Thank you to Doug and the team at the Waverley for helping organise a surprise birthday party! Everyone was super helpful with everything including setting up karaoke on their projector! The hireable space is a great size and would recommend to anyone organising something for 30-50 people
Lovely, cozy pub with great food. Went on a Sunday and had the fish and chips. Great meal and was also able to watch the F1 Race. Table is a bit sticky, but it's a pub at the end of the day.

I was visiting London and every other spot was sold out for Sunday roast. Me and a group of friends came here and they happily served us at the end of the day. Food was class. Service was great. They were playing classic Motown music the entire time. Made me feel right at home.

name: En Root Peckham
address: En Root, 28 Peckham Rye, London SE15 4JR, UK

reviews.text: Amazing dinner with a varied menu, food was fresh and service was friendly. Very reasonable prices. We’ll definitely be back!

We managed to get the perfect outdoor table for 10 of us!!  Everything was delicious especially the plantain with tamarind and the tandoori wings! I also tried the watermelon beetroot juice which was sooo good too. Really recommend not just if you’re vegan :>

Delicious food, amazing chef was really lovely, felt sorry for the guy as he was having to do the job of two people. Dropping 2 stars as the waitress was completely incompetent and really spaced out 🍃🚬… The chef had to come and take our order in the end and had to keep reminding the waitress to wait the tables. She served us a juice saying that it was a  much smaller glass than usual and then finally brought us the wrong bill having no idea what we had ordered… Rather baffling lunch experience.

This place has the best vibes. I had the Masala Dosa meal and I practically inhaled it, it was so delicious. The Chaitini (Chai Espresso Martini) is absolutely gorgeous and I can’t wait to try the rest of the cocktails on offer here! The Rose and sea salt ice cream (vegan) was beautiful, and very refreshing after my meal. The staff were lovely too! I’l be back soon for sure :)

Hippie place with Indian fusion food. I tried their raja & mushroom wraps. Both were quite unique and flavorful. I also loved the food presentation.

The staff was sweet and offered good service. They also have WiFi.

reviews.text: Visted Just Fab Kitchen with my little one, we both really enjoyed the make your own option. The owner is really friendly and helpful. A good range of dietary options. Will definitely be back.

Athreeh is so so so so lovely! Love seeing him every time we come and get our standard rum punches. He makes them nice and STRONG ta rassss yeah. Always serves with a smile and treats us nice as his loyal customers! Definitely come down here and play some pool and let him take care of your drinks (and funny chat) :D

I got served by Athresh at the Peckham Marketplace bar - went a couple of times for the rum punch! Really recommend it, great service and super friendly staff! The rum punch was strong and delicious and we got a half price deal. Really recommend a visit if you are looking for a comfortable place where to have a drink!

** New update from last year. Added some more photos of the tacos I tried this time around **

It's a short walk from Peckham Rye Station on the train and plenty of choices of bus routes to access the location, somewhere a bit different also.

They did to my surprise have x 5 pool tables which were ace too.

The music choice and atmosphere would be my only criticism, needs more of a vibe on that front and the second time around they were showing the footy, so that's good to keep in mind too.

Nice bar area and plenty of drinks to choose from.

Solid A****

address: 89 Peckham High St, London SE15 5RS, UK

reviews.text: I bought 2 sets of large rice n peas and jerk chicken yesterday and this was what was served to me. This is not the first time I have bought from them, so I find this really deceiving and very unacceptable. If there wasn’t enough chicken at that time it could have been communicated but to cheat the customer is very unacceptable. Probably a quarter chicken chopped into tiny pieces and split onto the two dishes. Second frame is the chicken that was served per dish. That lady should be ashamed. You guys should do better.

As soon as we stepped off the bus near Peckham Library, the irresistible aroma from Soul Fuel pulled us straight in you could smell the grill and that perfectly seasoned jerk chicken from a mile away.

We ordered the jerk chicken (sweet jerk sauce) with rice and peas, along with a refreshing fruit punch. The food was genuinely 10/10 rich, flavourful, and clearly made with love. The chicken was tender, juicy, and packed with that authentic smoky kick you’d expect from proper jerk. We even ended up taking extra home!

Service was fast, friendly, and efficient we didn’t have to wait at all. It’s proper homemade comfort food at its finest.

We’ll definitely be back to try more from the menu especially the mac and cheese, curry goat, and plantain. A true gem in Peckham highly recommended!

Had a lovely experience here. Food was spectacular and the flavours were immaculate. The gaot curry was melt in your mouth. Rice were perfectly cooked. Jerk chicken was spicy but packed with flavour, the good kind of spice😋. Totally worth it if your in the area. Staff were welcoming and friendly. Couldn't ask for a better than this.
I believe that, even in Jamaica you can't get this jerk chicken.😅
Thank you guys.

This place is deceiving as pictures and reviews suggest it’s good but it’s actually not very good.

Curry goat didn’t have great flavour and meat was not that tender and juicy.
The jerk chicken was okay but have definitely had better.
The food didn’t travel well in the takeaway boxes and leaked evrerywhere.
The rice and peas was stodgy and floury.
The price was too expensive for what it was.
Food preparation was slow.

The lady was friendly however.
And the portion was quite big.

It’s not like awful but I don’t think I’d recommend it to anyone or go again.

You can get much better Caribbean food, this one just had no wow factor.

Food is absolutely lovely here,very generous portions I had the curry goat it was tender no  bones, rice and peas were beautiful,came with salad and a drink for less than £10 bargain. My partner had the large curry goat was absolutely huge for extra £2.00 Highly recommend.

🚇 Peckham Rye
🍺 £6.90 Estrella Galacia

The Angel Oak is located opposite the top end of Peckham Rye Park in Peckham, southeast London. The nearest station is Peckham Rye.

This pub was built in the mid-19th century and was originally called The Rye Hotel, later becoming Rye House. In recent years, the pub was known simply as The Rye until it was refurbished and renamed The Angel Oak in 2021.

This is a large, one-bar, multi-room pub with a contemporary feel. The main bar area is located at the front and features a centrally positioned servery. The bar area has high ceilings and mixed seating, including benches, booths, and traditional tables and chairs. To the back left of the servery is a dining area, which then leads to a huge beer garden at the rear. The decor consists of boarded floors, bold pastel painted walls, an eclectic mix of prints and artworks, a few large Tv’s, and modern light fixtures.

The beer selection was solid and offered premium continental lagers and locally brewed craft beers. There were cask pumps, but they were not in use. I opted for an Estrella Galicia; my pint was great, price point was high. The food menu consists of pub classics — fish and chips cost £18, and roasts are available on Sundays.

I arrived at 5pm on a mild Saturday afternoon in August. The pub was absolutely packed throughout, with a predominantly younger crowd. There was a real upbeat buzz about the place while the Leeds v Newcastle match was showing live on the projector screen. The service was good; I didn’t have to wait too long to be served, and the team were coping well under pressure.

All told, this was an enjoyable pub visit — and it was great to see a pub so busy on a Saturday afternoon. My pint was spot on, the surroundings were comfortable, the beer garden was a big bonus, and the hospitality was pleasant. Be sure to check this one out if you’re in the area.

We had an incredible sunday roast! The food was very lovely and the beer selection was fantastic. We were looked after by Saffi, who was super friendly, attentive, and accommodating. Definitely one of the best roast spots around Peckham for sure. We will be coming back :)

I’ve been a regular customer at the pub for nearly three years, as I live just a two-minute walk away. I usually really enjoy the food – the chicken and bacon wrap at lunchtime is a favourite, and the burger is also very good (especially with added bacon).
However, I was quite disappointed with my experience today. I ordered the steak sandwich, which was unfortunately terrible – the meat was tough, completely flavourless, and practically impossible to chew. I also ordered a chicken sandwich for my daughter, which was just about acceptable, but the chicken was clearly dry and tasted as though it had been cooked several days ago.
It’s a shame, as I normally enjoy the food here, but today’s meal was well below the usual standard.

My family and I came here for Sunday roast to celebrate several family birthdays.  The food was absolutely amazing, the staff were brilliant and the service was excellent.  We have been a number of times before and would definitely come here again.

Had a lovely afternoon drinking pints here last week. Great chat with the bartender, Kwame, and the other punters were very nice and chilled too. Didn't have the food so unfortunately can't comment on that but will be coming back again to try it!

name: Jumbi
address: Unit 4.1, Copeland Park, 133 Copeland Rd, London SE15 3SN, UK

reviews.text: Such a sensational spot. The food was absolutely divine, honestly such incredible flavours. The drinks were creative and so tasty. Highly recommend the ginger beer shandy. The vibes later in the evening were also immaculate and became a really buzzing spot for a real mix of music. There were two rooms which had different vibes of music and an outside area. The entry for later at night was £7 pp

DONT BELIEVE THE HYPE… but kind of do.
This place has been all over my feed, probably yours too.

A bar and restaurant with a live DJ, teaming up with a jerk chicken kitchen, makes for a really fun night.

It’s far from polished in terms of decor, but it’s gorgeous. They’ve nailed the look. The wall of vinyl is a visual highlight and ties the space together.

Food’s decent but the menu’s quite niche, likely down to a small kitchen. The taco-style flatbread was a standout: super spicy. The West Indian version of halloumi with honey was also excellent & still thinking about it. The rest was fine, nothing special.

Cocktails were a mixed bag. The rum and raisin espresso martini was brilliant; their old fashioned, not so much, bad glass, poor presentation, and overpriced for what it was.

Staff were friendly and cool but service was slow, especially for ordering another drink. And only one dessert on the menu? Odd choice.
Beautiful venue. The dumpling starter is AMAZING. Plantain I thought was quite average. Service is good, but slightly slow. Nice for a date night 😚
The Sunday Roast is so gooood! Chicken and Lamb both delicious. Their signature cocktails also 10/10. The place also looks really nice. Forgot to take a picture of the food and drinks.

I went here yesterday with my wife. It was a place I always wanted to go to, because they do an infusion of dishes which is Jamaican & Turkish, called Jurkish. I must say, I was not disappointed. We tired most things on the menu and we enjoyed them all. The standout dishes for me were the Plantain Falafel and Saltfish Badadez Kofte. We also had some delicious cocktails.

From start to finish everything was wonderful! Do yourself a favour and book.
Starting from the top, our sever Molly was great! She made us feel very welcome, explained the menu and didn't try to oversell and make us over order as you see in a lot of other restaurants. Her recommendation were spot on. Everything we order was impeccable. The dishes were well timed in between. Food was delicious and the cocktaila were great too.
We took our time and while there was a booking right after us, we didn't feel rushed. We were welcomed to have a drink (and any potential desert) in the other part of the restaurant. Which was lovely.
Great music selection, friendly staff, great drinks, incredible food. I'm very excited for my next visit. It's another beautiful gem in Peckham that fits so well here. Thank you!

My favourite restaurant in London. The menu is extremely creative and changed a lot - so even though I visited multiple times I always got to try new and exciting dishes. Especially their fish and seafood based dishes are exceptional!

Staff is very welcoming and the service is superb. Also for this quality of cuisine it’s good value for London-standards!

I’ll definetely keep visiting :)

Lovely setting in the old station building, innovative and creative menu with a great drinks menu to accompany.

The menu has a wide range of interesting dishes, some classics with a modern twist and fresh ingredients.

The setting is quirky and trendy, a small intimate dining space and a fantastic team.

A true gem of a place in SE15!

Just had dinner at Hausu Peckham and it absolutely delivered. The food was excellent across the board, but the standout for me was the ox heart ragù - rich, deeply savoury and cooked to perfection. The side of potatoes deserves a special mention too: simple, golden and ridiculously moreish.

The vibe is warm and sociable, the kind of place that feels instantly lively and welcoming. It does get quite loud once it fills up, so not one for hushed conversations but perfect if you’re after a buzzy, shared-table energy.

Would happily go back (and order that ragù again in a heartbeat).

An amazing intimate dining experience and a cosy atmosphere.

Food was so unique and delicious, I would definitely recommend getting a little bit of everything.

Friendly and warm staff.

Highly recommended.

name: Patty Bro’s
address: Market Place Peckham, Unit 10, The Aylesham Centre, Rye Ln, London SE15 5EW, UK

reviews.text:
Today i tried their Chicken burger , it was outstanding and delicious.

I must say their customer service is so good and polite.

Best smash burger in town, i urger all the people  to try their burger.
Amazing freshly made smash burgers and fries! Super friendly service and good size portions.

The CHICKEN BURGER  is comfort wrapped in warmth tender, juicy, and gently seasoned, offering a familiar hug with every bite. It’s light yet satisfying, letting the flavors breathe without overwhelming the senses. A quiet classic that never disappoints.

The BEEF BURGER is bold and confident. Rich deeply satisfying, it delivers that unmistakable depth of flavor that feels indulgent and celebratory. Each bite is hearty and soulful, a reminder of why this burger remains an all time favorite.

The VEGGIE BURGER is a pleasant surprise vibrant, thoughtful, and full of character. Packed with texture and layered flavors, it proves that plant-based can be just as exciting and fulfilling. It’s fresh, creative, and quietly impressive.

Together, these burgers form a perfect harmony comfort, strength, and innovation sharing the same plate, each shining in its own delicious way. 🍔✨

I recommend people to visit the shop and try by yourself.

The meal deal is priced at £14 and offers excellent value for money. The burger was genuinely one of the best I’ve had in London. The service was outstanding (10/10) and the staff were extremely polite and professional. A thoroughly enjoyable experience.

You wanna grab a burger around Peckham???
Patty Bro’s is the place where you head to.
Cool amazing vibe to hangout with friends and family. Tremendous service from the boys too 🫡 The best 👍

A hidden vegan gem in South London (Peckham). A small and cosy place, I was not quite hungry so I had just a empanada, which was really delicious (and the sauce was so spot on), and a dessert, the macaroons served with cinnamon, nutmeg, a candy compote fruit and a reduction of pomegranate, and almond flakes. Beautifully served and exquisite. I have to go again and try everything!!

Vegan heaven!  Amazing food and exceptional service — I can wholeheartedly recommend this place to both vegans and non-vegans. I keep coming back because the dishes are genuinely addictive. From the crispy, flavorful empanadas to the comforting vegetable casserole that tastes like a warm hug, everything is outstanding. The deserts that are literally the best vegan desserts that I had in my life! The owner is always so friendly and welcoming! 10/10

Delicious vegan cakes! Tried the mini almond ones with parsnip jam, very good, something I have never tried before, not to sweet, just right. All the cakes were delicious. The place is hidden in a local mini market but worth coming to! The owner was super nice and warm, I am definitely coming back for proper food.

A true gem! Delicious, freshly prepared homemade food - the empanada pastry is so crisp, flaky and perfect - and wonderful, warm service from Bregary (the owner and chef). I've also tried the Charquicán (Chilean stew), bean burger, cakes and dessert - all so good. Every dish is presented beautifully and with such care. You feel nourished by the food, but it is also such a treat. Cannot recommend highly enough - not just for vegans/vegetarians, but for everyone!

So so so delicious, best empanadas I’ve had, and they’re made fresh to order. The quality of ingredients and balance of flavours is outstanding.

The dishes are on par (or better) with what you would get at a posh restaurant (for a lot more money). The selection of cakes and pastries great. The owner and chef is so lovely too and clearly passionate about good quality food and ingredients.

Everything was perfect and delicious!
Thank you to Rima and the girls for guiding us through the menu. The dishes were amazing and the ambience warm and welcoming. Slightly overpriced, but overall a lovely experience.

We had:
Starter:
Betel leaf wrap of ginger, peanut, shallot, coconut, galangal, kapi, palm sugar (gf, veo)
Main:
Steamed bamboo shoots and chicken in banana leaf, acacia, lemongrass, chilli, coconut cream (gf)
Stir-fry of venison, oyster sauce, sugar snap peas, cherry tomatoes, ginger (gf)
Stir-fry of kallets, chilli, garlic, yellow bean sauce (ve)
Dessert:
Vietnamese drip coffee with condensed milk
Yam doughnuts, fig jam, icing sugar (gf, ve)
Milo cheesecake, espresso caramel, rice biscuit, caramelised banana

We visited the Begging Bowl on  30 January 2026. We saw it on Instagram and thought we would try it.

It is a sharing menu. We ordered the pork curry, the fried Sea Bass, the stir fried Venison , hispy cabbage, Jasmine and sticky rice and a prawn salad and 3 non alcoholic cocktails.

The food came out as cooked, which was fine, however,  the portions were small and came in small bowls. For example,  there were 3 of us and the small portion of pork curry meant we got 1. 5 of a small square each  the prawn dish had 4 prawns!

The prawn salad, fried sea bass and pork curry were okay, but I would hardly call it authentic food.
It was very packed and our waiter was friendly and she provided good service.
The cons were that it was expensive for what we got the bill was £146, which is a lot for what we got. The non alcoholic cocktails were £8 each.
I am glad we tried it, but it is not a place I would revisit, the hostess showed us not interest , even when we were leaving and she was next ro the door, which she didn't open.!
I wish them well and I guess it is okay for a meal with friends,  but we will not be going back. £146 for 3 people, for small bowls in Peckham.
A fab Thai restaurant with some great vegan options. All the dishes were fresh and flavoursome, and great for sharing.   Not cheap but well worth a visit if you’re in the area.

We came with children for family lunch to experience new Thai flavours but instead we left hungry with £100 in our pocket… Very disappointed… my daughter ordered pomelo salad which was a main course and was around £13, we needed to look for pomelo in the salad… everything was very spicy and flavourless… We were expecting vibrant colours of vegetables and rich flavours like we have had experience in different places. Who is creating cold main dishes in winter? I have ordered prawns and they were cold and covered with bed of ginger shoots and other vegetables which I don’t know the name. Beautiful place and have so much potential if the food will be tasty.Very disappointing. We want be back for sure. By the way who is giving the name: “Begging bowl” for the restaurant. To be honest the name speaks for itself!

I adored The Begging Bowl 🍲. The vegan selection was incredible, and everyone enjoyed the plant based dishes 🥦. The wine was delicious 🍷. The server went to special effort to get some white that was chilled 🧊.

We had almost one of everything 🍽️. We ordered more of what we liked, and the dishes were brought to the table really quickly ⚡. Favourites were the pumpkin and celeriac curries 🥘. Another favourite was a layered potato appetiser that was incredible 🥔.

I would have loved pudding if I was not so full 🍮.

5/5 stars

name: 19FiftySeven
address: 660 Old Kent Rd, London SE15 1JF, UK

reviews.text:
An authentic taste of home

19fiftyseven Restaurant is a cosy, welcoming spot on the Old Kent Road serving beautifully presented, authentic Ghanaian dishes.

I visited on a Sunday evening and was pleasantly surprised by how easy it was to find parking on a nearby side street. From the moment we arrived, we were warmly greeted by the owner, Geoffrey, an absolute asset to the establishment. He seated us promptly and provided a QR code for the digital menu.

As we made our selections, the nostalgic sounds of Daddy Lumba played softly in the background, instantly setting the tone and amplifying the authentic Ghanaian atmosphere. The décor is tasteful and thoughtfully done, with warm tones, Ghanaian-themed imagery, and elegant gilded cutlery subtly reinforcing the cultural theme without feeling forced.

We ordered chinchinga (lamb kebabs) and kelewele (spicy fried plantain) to start, followed by omo tuo (rice balls) with groundnut soup and banku (fermented corn and cassava dough) with okra stew.

What truly stood out for me, beyond the food and the setting, was the warmth of the owner. We spent much of the evening putting the world to rights, chatting about Ghana, business, culture, and life, the kind of easy conversation that makes you feel more like a guest in someone’s home than a customer in a restaurant.

I cannot recommend this place enough. The food is excellent, the hospitality genuine, and the atmosphere relaxed and authentic. It delivers on all levels.
The private function room downstairs is an added bonus and is most definitely something I plan to make use of in the future.

Overall: a solid 5/5.

I was really looking forward to trying this local Ghanaian restaurant and supporting a business in the community. First impressions were great – the waiter was friendly, attentive and well-versed in the menu. The restaurant was quiet when we arrived, with only one other couple dining but the music was extremely loud. I politely asked for it to be turned down and the staff kindly obliged.

Our starters arrived promptly, as did the children’s meal, which was absolutely lovely. Everything tasted fresh and well-prepared - a very promising start.

Unfortunately, things started to go downhill from there. After the starters were cleared, I was told my main would take around 10 minutes as the fufu needed to be freshly prepared – which was completely fine and appreciated. However, while one main course arrived, mine never followed. I ended up waiting 45 minutes and still had to ask for an update. After waiting over an hour in total, I had to cancel the dish as it still hadn’t arrived.

To make matters worse, as more people entered the restaurant, the music was turned up even louder than before. It became overbearing and people were forced to shout over the noise. The waiters had to lean in very close just to hear what diners were saying - it made the environment feel chaotic rather than enjoyable.

What made the situation more frustrating was that the restaurant never appeared to be especially busy - the manager or owner was outside socialising while delays were building inside.

I genuinely wanted this to be a standout experience. I make a conscious effort to support local businesses, especially those within my community. The starters were genuinely delicious and the children's meal was spot on. I personally wouldn’t order the jollof again but the children’s banku and okro soup was decent – I’d give it a 6/10.

It’s a real shame, because with a few simple changes, this place could be excellent. I really wished it had lived up to its potential.

I came here for the first time for a birthday dinner, and I absolutely loved it! I came on a Sunday and had the traditional menu - everything was so delicious and beautifully presented. The lamb kebabs, chicken and jollof all had so much flavour! The bofrot for dessert was also incredible! 😍 The decor is lovely and the staff were so attentive and friendly. I loved the traditional music too which made you feel like you were in Ghana! I'd highly recommend and cannot wait to come back again! 😊

Quaint and just right. Big sitting area downstairs for large parties.
Food was 10/10 banging, we ate so much and were comatose by it.
The palm wine was just perfect in the calabash for original way to drink it touch🤩

Maybe just went on a bad day. The positives were good starters. The lamb kebabs in particular are really good. The rest of the experience was unfortunately sub par.

Service was extremely slow in taking orders and serving starter. Despite the slow turnaround, our drinks still didn’t reach us until after the starter was served. That should never happen. The drinks offer a restaurant respite from the wait for a starter so delaying it only exacerbates the feeling that service is being slow. We wanted second drinks but chose not to order as it would take too long.

The menu is reassuringly small but when that is the case, you can’t have two of the six mains unavailable that day, particularly if they’re two of the more appealing choices. What we ended going for wasn’t particularly inspiring or enjoyable to eat. So we skipped dessert.

The restaurant looks the part and has a good atmosphere but some simple stuff needs to be improved.
It was my first time at Ganapati, and we were absolutely delighted with the food. The starters were amazing, and we shared a couple of mains that were just as delicious. We can’t wait to go back!

Great restaurant, the foods amazing, friendly staff and loved the dimly lit ambience. They must be doing something right as they have been open for 20 years. Need to book in advance as they are always busy.

The food was amazing as was the hospitality of the super friendly owner herself, the talented chefs and Johann our server.

He is an artist in the way he delivers the menu choices. We had decision paralysis as everything sounded so good. He asked what we liked, if we had any allergies and recommended dishes accordingly. Haven't seen anyone enjoy what they do in such a long while and also do it well!! He could sell water to a fish!

Would recommend.
Had fantastic Indian food here, with authentic flavours and a good variety of veg food. Don't miss the beetroot dosa or the dal paneer with paratha. I'm surely going back again.

There were 20 of us at the weekend for our dad's 86th birthday and the team couldn't have been more accommodating! Johann handled everything perfectly including managing 6 children and ordering a selection for all the adults. The food was delicious (as always) and everyone was very happy! Would go again in a heartbeat!

name: Francesco’s Panino ( Previously called Francesco Chicken )

reviews.text: The owner is nice and friendly. The price is insanely good. The taste is amazing. Would recommend 👍

WOW!!! This place is seriously unreal. My brother and I usually go to Francesco’s for pizza, but one of the staff there told us this is their go-to spot for coffee and sandwiches… and now we know why. We got the chilli honey panino and the tagliatelle bolognese for just £11 and it absolutely blew us away. So much flavour, perfectly done, and insane value. Already planning to come back tomorrow 😋🔥
This is one of the best spots in Camberwell!! Such good value for money, and genuinely tasty sandwiches! The bread that they use is delicious, and definitely rivals Gladwell’s and Toad Bakery bread

Very dissapointed. Not quite sure how the reviews are so high. Was very poor. Bland,cold chicken in the sandwich. Very big sandwich but the taste and quaIity was poor. I struggled to eat more than a third of it as it was so poor. Morley's across the road is much better value. Maybe it was an off day but I can't recommend this place at all
10/10. The owner is very friendly and the food is top notch. The best french fries in london also.

name: Viet Quan
address: 320 Old Kent Rd, London SE1 5UE, UK

reviews.text:
We went on a Sunday, around 7pm the restaurant was very clean, the staff were very nice and friendly.
We ordered:
- chicken wings £9.50 (you get 3 pieces, it was just normal fried chicken 3/5)
- squid £10.50 (the portion was not as much there was 5 of us, we probably needed another portion, for us it was a little too salty 4/5)
- classic Pho (you can’t go wrong with a classic Pho, portion was perfect)
- signature hue soup (I got medium spice level, I still added more chilli, so delicious and the portion was also perfect)
- chicken wok pho (super super flavourful!! Honestly so tasty! Portion was amazing very big)
- beef curry (the beef curry was nice, however there was more potato/ carrots than the actual beef but very flavourful as well, portion was good for one and also came with rice!)

We actually had a little tiny accident and the staff were very nice, didn’t make a fuss and replaced the drink for free which was very kind. The staff are very nice and have good music taste hehe!
We ordered many menus to try and I like Mango salad and Pho 🍜 noodles. They are big portions that you can share with family and friends

The restaurant is spacious and quiet not busy at all. The Vietnamese coffee is decent though I would ask for less ice next time as most of the glass was filled with ice. The pho is quite oily and could have had more flavour. I would come here again if I was passing by.

Used to be very decent place but my last order was a disaster. Spring rolls were so disappointing. no herbs, no mint, basil, nothing. Super bland with so few prawns it was just sad looking. Genuinely terrible effort.
Crispy chicken and rice was another sad meal. With not even a hint of "crisp", again bland, and with a very unbalanced sauce.
Classic Pho was ok, but lacked depth. It was ok.
Overall I definitely won't be returning.

One of the best Vietnamese restaurants in London area. Much more spacious than some venues i have been before. You can also find some local dishes here which are hard to find anywhere else in london area. Good service and fair price.

I'm currently learning Georgian and about Georgian culture. This place is lovely Tornike and Hannah were very attentive with amazing reccomendations for Georgian wine. I had the Kissi orange wine, it was delicious!! All their wine is organic, with Georgia being the birthplace of wine, you know you're getting only the best. Today I had just some khachapuri and orange wine but I've been here before and had a full spread, everything is freshly made, the khachapuri is so moreish, the khinkali is amazing. They have gorgeous fresh salads and dips to accompany everything. With lit candles and a beautiful interior overlooking a pretty common, it's a wondwrful date spot or way to spend an evening.

This establishment has subtly become one of our go-tos, and the place we'll invariably visit when in the vicinity of southern Peckham and keen for gustatory indulgence. Gazing into the other Rye eateries after departing 80-20, one is struck by how much of a better time one has almost certainly had. Better service from the endlessly charming gentleman who runs the place, better food from the magnificent lady whose khachapuri, khinkali and tapas deserve to be famous among the suburbanites of central South London, better atmosphere and certainly better wine, with no menu bottle exceeding £40 and many not exceeding £30, all of utterly exceptional quality and with staggering variety to boot (more adventurous options from the shelves are also available). Our host will freely recommend something delicious and even, as we're regulars, offer complimentary tastes of amber or semi-sweet wine; one of the latter has become our ever-reliable friend, but tonight's amber was of such quality that I've pledged to get it next time. We were also this time (our fifth visit I think) treated to a free double-scoop of their excellent gelato, although I don't see myself betraying their kada quite yet. Would kada work with ice cream? One for next time, probably. Tonight's khinkali were utterly superb, and there is an array of both traditional and somewhat adventurous tapas (heavily featuring ajika sauce) that I'd certainly urge the explorative diner towards, but no greater pleasure, no purer treat perhaps on this earth exists than the khachapuri adjaruli one can obtain here, and I'd include the khachapuri at every other Georgian restaurant in London in that (we've been to a few!) - I mean, we've never had a bad experience at a Georgian restaurant, and it must be stressed that this nation's astounding cuisine and viticulture is responsible for 80% of the joy of coming here. But the 20%? That crucial edge? That's the hospitality, knowledge and skill of the two people who run the show. We'll inevitably return soon, and hopefully a few other Londoners vacillating on how to spend their hard-earned disposable income will read this and make the needful beeline!

I had an amazing experience at this restaurant. The food was incredibly delicious, and the wine was absolutely fantastic. Every dish was full of flavor and beautifully presented.
The service was also top level friendly, attentive, and professional from start to finish. You can really feel the passion and care in every detail.
I highly recommend this place to anyone looking for great food, excellent wine, and a memorable atmosphere. I will definitely be coming back!

Went there on a Friday for dinner, a group of four with prior reservations (which I would recommend on the weekends). They have a really good selection of Georgian wine, and the people there very friendly and knowledgeable. Before getting into details, my biggest complaint was the speed and the other of the service: our food arrived slowly (and they had told us that we could order as we go if the food wasn't enough, which would have taken ages), and in the "wrong" order. That said, it could have been because they were busy, but I would gladly go there again to see whether they've ironed these issues out.

I'm not completely sure about names of the plates, so apologies for any mistakes here. We ordered the Georgian Cheese bread (Khachapuri), which they suggested the salad as an excellent accompaniment, as well as the Khinkalies (dumplings), and the tapas.

They came with the salad first, but nothing else. We sat there waiting for a while, and they noticed that and asked us if all is ok. The salad is meant as a side salad, which isn't really a dish in and of itself, and they had recommended it for the bread. Eventually, we got hungry and had the salad. Then after a while the dumplings came, which were good but could have been better filled (I've had really good Khinkalies  in London before). Then came the bread after a long wait: very cheesy, but the bread could have risen a bit more. Finally after having waiting even more, we finally got the tapas. The meat in the tapas was a bit dry, and the halloumi cheese, while good, isn't really Georgian.

The wine they suggested to go with the food was good. Like I said, all in all we were happy, and hopefully it'll be better the next time.

Not impressed.
I’m a big fan of Georgian food but this is not to the level.
Georgian salad was just not fresh (they agreed and didn’t even charge for it)
Khachapuri was not bad.
Khinkali were 3/5. The dough was too thick, not enough sauce inside, and actually slightly undercooked.
The wines were good and the waiter was nice.

name: The Red Bull
address: 116 Peckham High St, London SE15 5ED, UK

reviews.text:
The Red Bull used to be one of my favourite pubs in Peckham. A quiet, unassuming spot hidden in a busy part of South East London. It was the kind of place you could rely on for a relaxed pint without too much chaos.

It’s recently changed management and has taken on a more Irish-focused identity, which has clearly given it a new lease of life. It’s genuinely great to see it so busy!

I’ve popped in a few times since the change. I’ve had a Guinness and tried the spice bag/munchie box. The beer selection is ok. The food was nothing particularly memorable.

For me, though, it’s lost that calm, low-key charm that made it such a regular haunt. It now feels more geared towards lively student crowds and split-the-G energy than a quiet catch-up over a drink.

So fair play to them, it’s clearly working. It’s just not quite my kind of pub anymore.

Really great atmosphere on a Friday night here, everyone is jovial and singing along to whatever is being played on the speakers. Drinks are well priced and are well poured. Had the spice bag share box when I came which was nice for about half before it became a bit stodgy so I’m not in a rush to return back for. Good Peckham pub.
Thursday nights trad music was amazing! Great Guinness pours too

🚇 Peckham Rye
🍺 £5.80 Cruzcampo

The Red Bull is located opposite Manze’s Pie & Mash shop on busy Peckham High Street. The nearest station is Peckham Rye, it’s only a few minutes walk to get here.

There has been a pub on this site since the 17th century, the building you see today was built in 1880. This pub closed in the late 1970’s and has had multiple uses including most recently a hair dressers. Thankfully the pub reopened in autumn 2019 and then became Barefoot Joe's Bar for a while, in April this year the pub reinstated its original name.

This is a one bar pub with traditional furniture plus a few remnants from the previous bar incarnation. The servery is located on the back wall and has a solid wood counter. Around the walls are beautiful glazed Victorian tiles which are slightly hidden by the seating. The standout feature which was such a surprise to find was the stunning tiled mural of “The Trial of Queen Katherine". For the warmer months, there are benches at the side of the pub.

The beer lineup was all keg and featured a couple of craft beers. I decided on a pint of Cruzcampo, my pint hit the spot, price point was just below average. The food offering is Pizza, there are 9 to choose from, most cost around a tenner. There is a deal where you can get a Pizza and a Pint for £14.

We arrived around 8pm on a warm Saturday evening in July. The atmosphere was chilled with a few locals in attendance. I got chatting to the Guv’nor and his good Lady who were telling me all about their vibrant locals boozer. They also showed me a book detailing the historical importance of the tiled mural.

The pub hosts a variety of events and promotions, keep an eye on their socials for what’s on.

Peckham has had a devastating loss of pubs over the last twenty years, so it was great to visit this pub that is back from the dead. This is a welcoming local with lovely people at the helm. The tiled mural was amazing, the beer and pizza are reasonably priced. Well worth a visit if you’re in the area.

ℹ️ Info correct on visiting 27.07.24
The perfect Guinness, excellent food from Scaldy, great atmosphere, friendly staff

name: Kix Bar + Kitchen
address: Kix Bar + Kitchen, 57 Lordship Ln, London SE22 8EP, UK

reviews.text: We love Kix for a mid week or Saturday  night  cocktail and meal and until last weekend had never tried the Sunday roast. We remedied this last weekend and had a fantastic Sunday lunch with our two daughters. We couldn’t resist the starters and so shared the tuna tartare (utterly amazing and the tempura leaf it was plated on was culinary genius!) and the fancy nachos - both were delicious. Roasts of miso glazed chicken and beef sirloin followed with the most incredible creamy  leeks, duck fat roasted and Yorkshires (regardless of what you ordered) and proper gravy in abundance.  Utterly delicious and served up with spicy margaritas and plenty of wine! The team at Kix are some of the friendlist I’ve encountered and the ambience is gorgeous. Totally worthy of a visit or five - a real gem!

Lovely find that led to a lovely evening. Friendly and helpful staff, really nice atmosphere. Quality food. Looks good. Also, sweet potatoes are the best in London. It’s not just some fried sweet potatoes, there’s science behind it! Spanish Basque Cheesecake was amazing.

The restaurant has great vibes and the staff are great- attentive, friendly and helpful. The cocktails were delicious-perfect margaritas! Food was nice and portion sizes were good! Tuna tartar was the stand out dish for me!
Food and cocktails were really good. The place has a good fun vibe. I would comeback for dinner but also just for drinks.

I had some delicious margaritas and food (the corn ribs and steak are amazing!) at the lovely Kix. I would definitely go back! the staff were really polite and knowledgeable and the vibe in there is great. 🖤

name: Queens SE15
address: Unit 35, Railway Arch Astbury Business Park Station Passage, Arch 131 Station Passage, London SE15 2JR, UK

reviews.text:
Lovely Italian wine selection!
Great food on the menu and specials off the menu (try the Giambota!!)
And the service is Second to None!
Finally Peckham has a place like this ❤️

**Poor staff training and poor manners**

My husband went to this place around 5.30pm to ask if children where allowed, the place being near to empty. A staff member assured him that we would be most welcomed.

Once we got there with our children, the owner with incredible insensitivity denied us from entering saying the children were not allowed due to the licence. I questioned what kind of licence was he referring to considering it was before 9pm and that they sell food. He stoically responded his own licence. So I said that it's not the license but "his choice". He agreed. One of our children cried all the way home as she felt so upset about how we were treated. She apologised for being a child.

I am personally sick and tired of this discrimination towards families. Have we not all been children at some point? Does the owner of this place have a heart somewhere? Are children not integral part of our society or are they animals? Does he realise London and SE15 likes inclusive businesses and that it's year 2025!?

You sell pastries and coffee.... why are children denied entrance?

One could have said they were booked and explained quietly that children cannot go after a certain time, or have a clear sign.

Better staff training and politeness would have avoided such a very unpleasant encounter.

Great party venue with superb food, excellent music and great all round venue. A gem of a place hidden in the arches
of Peckham, conveniently situated next to the station. Highly recommended.
Finally a decent place in Peckham! Was there last week, outstanding food and drinks and a really pretty place, very efficient and friendly staff too.

Antipasti and pizzas are a flawless 10/10. The prices are very reasonable, especially for the generous portions. The atmosphere is enhanced by great music, and the staff are exceptionally friendly, making every visit a pleasure.

name: The Greyhound - Peckham
address: 109 Peckham High St, London SE15 5SE, UK

reviews.text: Natty can cook's roti appetiser with scotch bonnet butter was delicious. The roast looked very pretty and appealing. The lamb chops were nice and well seasoned. The turkey wing was ok but needed to marinate a little longer. The veg, plantain and Yorkshire puddings were nice and the gravy was thick and flavoursome. The pub is a bit too cosy and was very busy; I can see how Natty may have outgrown the venue. The service at the bar was a little slow but the rum punch was generous and served in a pint glass.

I’m going to say, Nattycancook at the greyhound pub offered the best dining experience I’ve had in a while (and I’ve been to very expensive restaurants in the past). The food and drinks were great (8/10) and the service and atmosphere were exceptional (10/10). We had such a brilliant time.

We ordered The Lux, which had 5 different meats on the board, fried plantain, rice and peas, mac and cheese balls, roast potatoes and tempura broccoli. Drinks, we each had a Tutti Fruity and that was perfect, I would taste the Wray and Nephew so I knew I wasn’t been scammed out of watered down alcohol as most places seem to do these days.

The lamb chops, lobster tail, roast potatoes and mac and cheese balls were our favourite things on the board. The rice and peas was nice but didn’t taste authentic in our opinion. We put that down to Natty’s creative flair (plus, every Caribbean has a grandma who they’d say has the best food anyway).

For dessert, we had the lemon cake and custard and the red velvet cheesecake. We loved the lemon cake - it was super light! The red velvet cheesecake, we did not like. It was unusual…I still ate it but I wouldn’t recommend.

I CANNOT WAIT for him to have an established restaurant of his own. I absolutely recommend. 1000/10.

Lovely staff, great affordable pint selection the greyhound is really a pillar of the community and with the addition of patio pizza this is going to be a really special place, that guy KNOWS his pizza.

The snap on the crust is unreal, I’m so happy we’re getting a greater variety of pizza in London, neopolitan has been done as good as its ever gonna get, time for some new blood!
Such a cosy pub, and Patio pizza is so delicious. By far my favourite pizza in London. So worth it !!!!

I and my partner had a random day..an afternoon pint in a random pub..and it didn't disappoint  ,sampled some new stouts ,wow..talked to staff..great afternoon.then went back in the evening..vibes were fantastic,met so many people,music was so cool.had a awesome time.a must pub to visit at weekends

name: Rotorious
address: Unit 10, Market Stalls, 133a Rye Ln, London SE15 4BQ, UK

reviews.text:
Probably the best rotisserie chicken I have ever had!
A quarter chicken made me happy with all that curry tasting gravy and delicious rice and coleslaw.
Absolutely delicious and great quick service too!
It’s located in the hall with other food options so perfect when going in groups.

Two really tasty plates of food from Rotorious  a quarter chicken with coconut rice, slaw and mango salad - and their special gravy;  and Rotorious Fries - spicy fries loaded with chicken and slaw. Very, very good 😋 😋

Went with my husband and we got a big selection of food! It’s all gluten free which is a game changer as normally I’m restricted when getting fried chicken. You would never guess it was GF, the chicken was so tender and the batter was crispy and fresh!
The salad was also delicious, would recommend every single dish we got!!
Their version of peri peri sauce was absolutely banging and I wanted to take some home with me!
Highly recommend, cool chilled Peckham vibes too.
Delightful rotisserie chicken. Highly recommend the chicken salad. The mango and avocado salad is deliciously unusual. Prices are very reasonable.

Very tasty chicken.
I ordered the half chicken with rice and veg and it was generous serving.
The chicken was succulent and tasty seasoned and the sauce is tasty too.
The chef and staff were very friendly as well.

Nice place to spend Saturday! Nice and relaxed atmosphere, had some amazing Indian food which they have on Saturday afternoons by local chef from Tava Rakh. A few pints of Guinness with friends by the fire, can’t get much better than that..

Skehans has such a great atmosphere and aesthetic, it’s easy to see why it’s been named best pub in London! The staff were all so so lovely as well.
We visited end of November and they were doing mulled wine with a free homemade gingerbread cookie which I loved.
We also ordered food from Tava Rakh which was doing a plant based Indian menu, this was absolutely amazing! Super looking forward to visiting again.

Skehans is a famous Irish pub. It topped Time Out's 2023 "Best Pubs in London" list, being voted "London's No. 1 Bar." Their Guinness is guaranteed to be authentic and flawless. But I've quit drinking.
This pub is part of a joint venture with the Thai restaurant next door, so you can enjoy authentic, home-style Thai cuisine right there. The fried noodles were delicious, and the steak was even better than I expected—high-quality meat, though the tom yum gong was a bit too salty.

It's very lively and down-to-earth. I love the lively yet relaxed atmosphere; you can just chat with anyone you meet.
Great pub! Pub quiz on a Tuesday is also good but does get bloody packed! Ads to the atmosphere I guess but only issue is the £10 minimum spend on card, kinda annoying but one of my fave places

Hate, hate, HAAATE to be this person but unfortunately I have to be. I can't stand bad service any more than I can't stand in heels. A pub based in nunhead charging a stupid minimum £10 on card (basically a massive middle finger to anyone who isn't a raging alcoholic). The bar staff are few and far between in terms of being nice, they honestly would rather serve the wall than be nice to you and its actually quite ridiculous considering they want you to spend a fortune before you can tap your Google wallet. I had more genuinely nice interactions with the security guards than I did with any of the staff who worked there. I had incredibly high hopes for the food but honestly, I should've just lowered my expectations to hell because I basically filed my teeth on the calamari and in regards to the steak? I might as well have cut brick with the bloody butter knife they gave me, it would've probably done more with said brick than the cardboard cheap meat they served me.

The only reason I gave this place a chance despite hearing awful stories from family and friends who have been there, was for the aesthetic and the vibes. Unfortunately, I can't rip into them about the visual aesthetic and the live entertainment. That is good. I have to say. I also think the security guards are sweet and do a decent job of being friendly while ensuring the safety of the establishment.

If only good security and decorations could make this a good pub. Save your 10 quid in cash and go to the Pyrotechnists or the Nuns Head. ✌️

name: The Camberwell Arms
address: 65 Camberwell Church St, London SE5 8TR, UK

reviews.text:
Enjoyed my birthday dinner here and had a lovely time.

The scotch bonnet pork fat on toast was so good, I just wish I could’ve had 10 of them.

The broccoli “cacio e Pepe” with toasted buckwheat was good and did remind me of eating a cream pasta. The sauce was great to eat with bread too!

The fish, which I now can’t remember what it was, was so delicate, zesty and delicious. The mash was creamy and smooth and the combination of everything on the plate was perfect.

They kindly gave me a birthday surprise of rhubarb spritz sorbet ice cream

This a double review. One for the restaurant in general, which is reliably one of the best restaurants south of the river. The menu is always innovative and fresh but with classic cuisine at it’s heart. The staples that are always there like beer onions on toast, their incredible focaccia and their legendary Sunday roasts are always a 10/10.
The second half of the review is for Camberwell Arms’ catering of our wedding reception. Throughout the engagement Matilde was very easy to contact and thorough with the process of helping us select the menu and plan the day. After much back and forth customising the menu, at our tasting we were made to feel right at home and finished off with a further session with the chef to add any other bespoke elements to the dishes that had been prepared. This included a last minute request for a spare rib based canapé which was fulfilled and was the star of the pre dinner reception!
The food for 75 people which included their famous porchetta and a show stopping Paris Brest was served on the day with no hiccups whatsoever.
The night was finished with their sfincione which was also a hit and was completely hoovered up by the guests.
I can’t recommend Camberwell arms highly enough - whether it’s for a wedding, an evening dinner with friends or a Sunday roast.

The Camberwell Arms is one of the most reliable pubs for excellent food and warm service in south London. The menu is generous and seasonal, with dishes that feel both comforting and refined. The dining room has an easy, unpretentious charm, and the staff strike the right balance between attentive and relaxed. It works just as well for a quiet dinner as it does for a larger gathering. Consistently delicious food and a welcoming atmosphere make it a standout neighbourhood favourite. Delicious sprouts, gotta love the crunch.

It's taken us a while to get a Sunday booking here, but after our recent meal I can see why they're so popular! We really enjoyed their refreshingly original take on a Sunday roast that still celebrates the flavours and ingredients of the season. We were particularly impressed at the portion of the main meats, which although pricey, provided very good value for money. I was very grateful that the staff were knowledgeable and confident on gluten free options - our waitress quickly brought over a menu marked up with hand written notes on what was safe and what could be accommodated. We were so full from the meal that we opted to share the peanut parfait for dessert, but it was so moreish we found ourselves wishing we had ordered two. Really looking forward to coming back again soon to this cozy and inviting pub.

I’m confused by all the good reviews and highly disappointed by the roast we had last Sunday. My friends and I arrived and were standing around for about 10 minutes without being greeted and without acknowledgment. We then told an employee we had a booking which took staff a while to figure out where we were sat. The decor is bleak and service slow. Waiting staff seemed confused, forgetting parts of our orders and brining the wrong cutlery or missing cutlery like steak knives for our meal. The food was cold, and I assume would’ve tasted better if hot but still seemed quite flavourless. My friends and I are all disappointing to have paid for the meal even though we had asked for the service charge to be taken off it still felt like daylight robbery. Would not recommend or go back for even just a pint tbh. Broccoli was basically just a thick stalk with tiny florets on it. Bloody Mary was super average. It’s a shame because we heard good things about this roast and were all so excited for it…

name: The Copper Tap
address: 190-193 Peckham High St, London SE15 5EG, UK

reviews.text:
Finally leaving a review..

Great bar and fantastic staff,
A little bit of a hidden gem. Really nice locals and clientele in general. Very welcoming.
THE BEST PINT OF GUINNESS IN PECKHAM!! Great service and the most friendly staff ❤️

Copper Tap may just be the best pub I’ve ever been to in my many years in this world.
Copious amounts of cute cocktails, full of the best cracking crowds. Wow, I can barely describe the fantastic atmosphere.
Board games
Beers
Babes
Thanks love you

And beautiful vibes.

10/10 recommend to a friend or a acquaintance. Or even a stranger.

Ok, I've got to be honest. For some reason, from the outside, the pub looks a bit intimidating. But as soon as you walk through the doors you're greeted by lovely friendly staff, a really nice looking pub and a really lovely atmosphere. They often do comedy nights which I've heard are great fun, it seems that this pub is a really lovely little secret in our neighbourhood.

I’ve recently just moved to Peckham and this pub is fantastic! The bartenders are always a great chat & so are the regulars too! It’s got a cozy, saloon type of feeling when entering the bar with almost a sports bar feeling, which is great. It’s definitely a must go to pub when going to Peckham. Also, dog friendly which is perfect!

The only thing is the outside area needs something to make it more eye catching as the first few times I didn’t know it was a pub going past it, apart from that I would highly recommend The Copper Tap! 9/10 Experience. Will be returning soon!

The Cherry Tree Pub is easily a five-star place. The staff members are incredibly friendly and attentive, making you feel welcome as soon as you walk in. The atmosphere is great for everyone—whether you’re meeting friends, spending time with family, or just popping in on your own for a relaxed drink.

Their menu is impressively diverse, offering both alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages alongside a good selection of food. The fish and chips are absolutely to die for—perfectly cooked and full of flavour. And you must try the brownies for dessert, especially with the scoop of vanilla ice cream on top that melts in your mouth. 🍨

Overall, a fantastic pub with great service, great food, and a warm, inviting atmosphere. Highly recommended! 🍻

We held our son’s first birthday at the pub and had such a lovely experience. The food was great and the service was excellent from start to finish. The room at the back was the perfect space for a small party and the team went above and beyond even helping us set everything up.

All of the staff were friendly and welcoming, which made the day feel really relaxed and special. A special shout out to Matt and Navan who looked after us so well and made sure everything ran smoothly.

Thank you to the whole team for helping make it such a memorable celebration for our family.

We recently celebrated our wedding reception at The Cherry Tree, and it was truly a wonderful experience. Mat and the entire team went above and beyond to ensure everything was perfect — from organising and setting up the decorations to making sure each of our guests felt welcomed and well taken care of. Their kindness, attention to detail, and genuine care made our day even more special. We are incredibly grateful for all the support we received and cannot thank The Cherry Tree team enough for making our celebration so memorable. I would recommend it 1000 times, again we can not thank enough the support and kindness from the whole team

We love this place Ina and Navin are so very welcoming! I am able to come here by myself with my dog and feel so safe! Food is great this place is child friendly and so dog friendly too! There is a lovely outside area really spacious we often watch the football here! Food is lovely defo rate the fish n chips and the Sunday roasts. great place to watch sport easy to see screens inside & outside. We rarely go anywhere else feels like home.

What can we say about the Cherry Tree? It's our local so we may be a bit bias but whenever the opportunity strikes you'll find us down here with the dog watching the football. They treat the dog like royalty, show all the sports, the staff are brilliant and we love the food. The beer garden is perfect on a sunny day and indoors is the cosy pub vibes everyone's after when it's a bit chilly outside. It does get a bit busy when the Hamlets are playing but the service is never impacted! Hand down the best pub in the area 🤜🏼🤛🏼

name: The Phoenix
address: Windsor Walk, Denmark Hill, London SE5 8BB, UK

reviews.text:
I had an appointment at the hospital on Saturday morning 28.2.26, so my daughter took me to lunch across the road at the Phoenix.  It was my first time there. The pub is larger than I expected and had seating outside, with electric heaters.  Inside one side was a dining area, and the other a bar with tables and seating.  On arrival we both ordered a hot chocolate, which was very rich and tasty.  I ordered chicken skewers with a sauce, which were tasty and good portion size, from the starter menu.  I also had a largar shandy. They had a good beer selection.  I met Amia she was attentive and very professional, and was able to answer any question asked regarding the menu.

Friar or frazia (sorry can’t rember her correct name) was behind the bar with a very happy disposition.  Both girls were really friendly and attentive.  Nice to see young people doing a great job with a great attitude.  We noted they have a quiz night and Dj night, so we enquired about it.  I think this pub must have a great atmosphere in the summer, so I will most probably go there again.  Overall my experience 10/10 well done girls.

If you’re anywhere near Denmark hill, The Phoenix is an absolute gem and easily earns a full 5 stars.

From the moment you walk in, the atmosphere is warm, welcoming, and relaxed exactly what you want from a local bar. The place strikes a great balance between lively and comfortable, making it perfect whether you’re catching up with friends or just popping in for a drink. 😂

What really made the experience stand out, though, was the service especially from Millie. Millie was the best server there, hands down. She was incredibly friendly, attentive without being overbearing, and genuinely made us feel looked after the entire time. It’s rare to come across someone who brings that level of energy and care to their job, and it made a huge difference to our visit. Absolutely amazing service.

On top of that, the prices are very good, especially for London. You get great value for what you’re paying, which makes it even easier to settle in and enjoy your time without worrying about the bill stacking up.

All in all, The Phoenix is a fantastic spot with brilliant vibes, great value, and standout service thanks in large part to Millie. Highly recommended, and I’ll definitely be coming back! ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Stopped by The Phoenix recently and it’s genuinely one of the better bars I’ve been to around this area — easily deserves 5 stars.

The place has a really easygoing feel to it. It’s lively enough to have a good atmosphere, but still chilled so you can actually relax and enjoy yourself. It just feels like a proper local spot where you’re comfortable straight away.

Big shoutout to Sam as well — Sam was the best server there. He was absolutely amazing the whole time we were there. Really friendly, quick to help, and just made everything run smoothly without any fuss. Service like that honestly makes such a difference to your night.

Another big plus is the prices. For London, they’re very good, and you actually feel like you’re getting your money’s worth.

All in all, great vibes, great value, and standout service from Sam. Would definitely recommend and will 100% be back. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Spent my Tuesday night out with friends who chose this pub. I’m not much of a drinker but my friends thought the drink prices are reasonable and I thought the service was great. That’s hard to find these days. Amia (hope I’m spelling it right) was amazing. She was helpful and polite and her banter kept us entertained all night! 10/10 would recommend.

We had a brilliant time at this pub. The food was delicious, came out quickly, and was great value for money. The lighting behind the bar was great made it much easier to see, which gave the place a really warm and welcoming atmosphere. Millie served us and was really friendly and helpful throughout. She made the whole visit even more enjoyable.

I had a brilliant time at the Prince of Peckham Pub — such a fun, buzzing spot right in the heart of Peckham! The atmosphere is warm and welcoming whether you’re meeting friends for drinks, grabbing some food, or staying late for music and dancing. The staff were friendly and attentive, which made the whole visit really enjoyable. Their cocktails are fantastic, perfect for starting the night right. The food is tasty and satisfying too, with jerk-inspired dishes that pack plenty of flavour. The interior has a great energy with plenty of space to relax, socialise

Highly recommend this place for anyone looking for a vibrant bar with great drinks, a lively crowd and memorable nights out!
